text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Telekom Malaysia promised a thorough investigation into alleged discrepancies in the award of a contract to Swedish telecoms firm LM Ericsson.
-- Malaysia's 1996 Consumer Price Index increased by 3.5 percent compared to 1995's, the Statistics Department reported.
-- No action will be taken against illegal foreign workers if they leave Malaysia by January 31, said Deputy Home Affairs Megat Junid Megat Ayob.

-- The setting up of Malaysia's first life reinsurance company by the first quarter is expected to reduce the outflow of reinsurance premiums by at least 20 percent a year, said Life Insurance Association of Malaysia president Ezamshah Ismail.

-- Malaysia's dream of achieving developed nation status will not be attainable without the high-technology area, Multimedia Super Corridor, said Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad in California where he is on a trade mission.
-- Local institutions of higher learning will be graded based on the quality of their teaching, curriculum and staff, said Education Minister Najib Abdul Razak.
